concept.title: The Midnight Interchange
concept.setting: A single moonlit train station suspended between worlds, where the 12:00 train never quite arrives and three puzzle spirits drift between five brass-and-glass rooms. Each night the clockmaker, Wren Tallow, must repair the station's failing mechanisms before the moon sets.
core_mechanics: Wind-and-set: spend mainspring charges to rewind broken clocks, each rewind nudges an adjacent room's puzzle state
Five-room loop: Waiting Hall, Lost Luggage, Signal Box, Platform 3½, and the Conductor's Office shuffle their hazards and gifts each run
Three spirit dialogues: the Stationmaster (riddles), the Porter (memory matching), and the Last Passenger (sliding-tile timetables) each request a specific repair
Tool drafting: between rooms, pick one of three brass tools (oil can, tuning fork, pendulum weight) that reshape how puzzles resolve
Moon meter: a single 12-minute timer ticks down as the moon crosses the skylight; finishing a spirit's request banks moonlight for the next run
Persistent ledger: solved repairs leave engraved cogs in the workshop, unlocking new starting tools and softer puzzle variants on future runs
concept.art_style: Hand-pixeled at 64x64 sprite scale with warm brass and midnight-blue glass palette, lantern bloom, gentle parallax steam, and ink-drawn UI on aged paper
concept.target_mood: Hushed, melancholic, and quietly hopeful — the feeling of a quiet platform at midnight where everything is broken but nothing is hostile
concept.description: A short cozy roguelike about Wren Tallow, a clockmaker tending a moonlit station between worlds. Twelve-minute runs across five rooms, three puzzle spirits, no combat — just brass gears, soft train ambience, and the slow rebuilding of a place that wants to be whole.
unique_selling_points: 12-minute runs designed for a single cup of tea
No combat, no failure state — only repairs that carry forward
Three hand-written spirits whose requests reshape the station each night
Lo-fi train-platform ambience as a core mechanic, not just background

world.name: The Midnight Interchange
world.description: A single moonlit train station suspended between worlds where the 12:00 train never quite arrives. Wren Tallow, a clockmaker, drifts between five brass-and-glass rooms each night, repairing failing mechanisms before the moon sets. Three puzzle spirits — the Stationmaster, the Porter, and the Last Passenger — wait among the lantern-bloom and gentle steam.
world.lore_summary: Long ago the Midnight Interchange served travelers crossing between waking worlds, its great brass clock keeping the threshold honest. When the 12:00 train failed to arrive one autumn night, the station slipped halfway out of time. Now its mechanisms wind down a little more each evening, and only Wren Tallow — last of the threshold clockmakers — returns to wind them. Each repaired cog is engraved into the workshop floor, a quiet ledger of nights the station almost became whole again.

regions.name: The Midnight Interchange
regions.description: A moonlit threshold station of brass fittings, midnight-blue glass, and slow drifting steam. Five rooms loop around a central platform beneath a great skylight that frames the crossing moon. The 12-minute moon meter ticks softly overhead, and lantern bloom catches every polished gear.

rooms.name: Waiting Hall
rooms.description: A vaulted hall of empty benches and a wall of departure boards whose letters quietly reshuffle. Brass chandeliers hang low, their pendulums all stopped at 11:59. This is where Wren arrives each night and where the moon meter first begins to tick.

rooms.name: Lost Luggage
rooms.description: Shelves stacked with travel cases that hum faintly, each tagged with a name no living passenger remembers. The Porter drifts here, asking Wren to match returning luggage to its forgotten owner through quiet memory pairs.

rooms.name: Signal Box
rooms.description: A cramped tower of levers, dials, and a wall-sized track diagram lit by oil lamps. Mainspring charges spent here rewind the signal clock, nudging puzzle states in the rooms on either side.

rooms.name: Platform 3½
rooms.description: A narrow platform tucked between Platform 3 and Platform 4 that should not exist. The Last Passenger waits here on a bench, holding a sliding-tile timetable that never quite finishes resolving. Steam coils in slow parallax across the tracks.

rooms.name: Conductor's Office
rooms.description: A small wood-paneled office stacked with logbooks, riddle-cards, and a stopped grandfather clock. The Stationmaster receives Wren here, trading riddles for repair tokens and engraving each completed cog into the workshop ledger.

points_of_interest: The Tool Draft Table (oil can, tuning fork, pendulum weight)

connections.description: A brass-framed archway draped in soft lantern light leading from the benches into the luggage shelves.
A narrow service door behind the shelves, ringing faintly with signal bells.
An iron stairwell descending to a platform that wasn't there a moment ago.
A varnished door at the platform's end, its frosted glass etched with a stopped clock face.
A short corridor lined with old timetables, completing the five-room loop back to the benches.
A hidden shortcut through a maintenance hatch beneath the departure boards, opened by a signal pass earned from the Stationmaster.
A luggage chute the Porter unlocks once enough memory pairs have been restored.

global_properties.art_style: hand-pixeled 64x64, warm brass and midnight-blue glass, lantern bloom, parallax steam, ink-on-aged-paper UI

quests.title: Wind the Arrival Clock
quests.description: The Arrival Clock in the Waiting Hall has stopped at 11:59 again. Wren must spend a mainspring charge to wind it and begin the night's run, then draft her first brass tool from the table beside the benches.

objectives.description: Spend one Mainspring Charge to wind the Arrival Clock and start the moon meter.
Choose one brass tool from the Tool Draft Table to carry into the loop.

quests.title: The Porter's Memory Pairs
quests.description: Three humming travel cases on the Lost Luggage shelves are searching for their owners' tags. The Porter asks Wren to match each case to its rightful name before the lantern dims.

objectives.description: Match three humming travel cases to their owner tags in the Lost Luggage shelves.
Receive the Porter's Brass Token, which unlocks the luggage chute to Platform 3½.
Strike the tuning fork to chime a single hidden pair (optional softening).

quests.title: Rewind the Signal Box
quests.description: The Signal Box's track diagram has gone dim and its levers stick at half-throw. Wren must spend mainspring charges to rewind the signal clock, nudging puzzle states in the rooms on either side.

objectives.description: Spend at least three Mainspring Charges at the signal clock to rewind it.
Align all four track segments on the wall diagram so the lamps burn steady.
Receive the Stationmaster's Signal Pass after the signal clock rings true.

quests.title: The Last Passenger's Timetable
quests.description: On Platform 3½ the Last Passenger holds a sliding-tile timetable that refuses to finish resolving. Wren must arrange the tiles into a valid departure before the phantom whistle fades.

objectives.description: Slide the timetable tiles into a coherent 12:00 departure pattern.
Lock one tile in place using a Phantom Ticket to ease the final slide.
Stand at the edge of Platform 3½ as the phantom whistle answers the solved timetable.

quests.title: Engrave the Workshop Ledger
quests.description: Before the moon sets, Wren returns to the Conductor's Office to deliver her solved riddle cards. The Stationmaster receives each one and engraves a new cog into the workshop floor — a quiet promise that tonight, the station almost became whole.

objectives.description: Deliver at least one solved Stationmaster's Riddle Card to the Conductor's Office.
Engrave a new cog into the workshop ledger floor.
Bank a vial of moonlight to carry into the next run.

quests.title: Three Spirits, One Night
quests.description: A rare alignment: fulfill all three spirits' requests within a single 12-minute run. The skylight will hold the moon a heartbeat longer, and the Workshop Ledger will engrave a triple cog — softening every puzzle in nights to come.

objectives.description: Complete the Porter's memory matching request this run.
Complete the Last Passenger's sliding-tile timetable this run.
Answer the Stationmaster's riddle and turn in the card this run.
Reach the Conductor's Office before the moon meter expires.

failure_conditions: Moon meter expires before all three spirit requests are completed

npcs.name: Wren Tallow
npcs.description: The last of the threshold clockmakers, Wren returns to the Midnight Interchange each night with a tin of mainspring charges in her apron pocket. She speaks softly, listens longer than she talks, and treats every stopped clock as a quiet apology she means to answer.
npcs.appearance: A slight woman in her late thirties wearing a heavy canvas apron over a midnight-blue work shirt, sleeves rolled to the elbow. Brass loupe pushed up into chestnut hair, oil-smudged fingertips, a leather tool belt of tiny instruments. Lantern-amber light catches the brass buttons at her cuffs.

fears: the night she fails to return
a station that finally stops humming
quirks: hums the same four-note phrase while winding springs
thumbs the engraved cogs underfoot before each run
personality.speech_pattern: soft, measured, often trailing into a half-finished thought

relationships.description: Wren treats the Stationmaster as a former teacher she never quite stopped studying under.
The Porter passed her her first brass token; she never forgot the weight of it.
Wren never asks the Last Passenger where she meant to go. She just sits with her until the whistle answers.

entries.activity: arrives, winds the Arrival Clock, drafts a tool
loops the five rooms repairing mechanisms
engraves the night's cog into the workshop ledger

ledger: A night that almost became whole.

npcs.name: The Stationmaster
npcs.description: A tall, dignified spirit who keeps the Conductor's Office and the workshop ledger. He trades hand-lettered riddle cards for engraved cogs and signs every Signal Pass with the same fountain pen he used the night the 12:00 train failed to arrive.
npcs.appearance: A translucent figure in a long midnight-blue coat with brass buttons, a brimmed cap pulled low, a pocket watch chain that fades into mist where the watch itself should hang. Lantern light passes through him like through frosted glass.

quirks: taps the stopped grandfather clock twice before speaking
signs every pass with a flourish that loops back on itself
claims not to know his own riddles
personality.speech_pattern: courteous, antiquated, fond of the conditional tense

relationships.description: Considers Wren the rightful keeper of the threshold, though he would never say so aloud.
They have shared the night shift for longer than either remembers.
He keeps a seat reserved for her, though she never sits in the office.

entries.activity: engraves cogs into the ledger floor

idle: A station is only as honest as its clocks.
greeting: Good evening, clockmaker. The ledger is listening.
riddle: A card, if you'd care to draw one.
I no longer know the answer myself, you understand.
engraving: A new cog. Mark the date.
The floor remembers what the timetables forget.

npcs.name: The Porter
npcs.description: A round-shouldered spirit who drifts the Lost Luggage shelves with a brass tag-lantern, returning humming travel cases to their forgotten owners. He presses a small brass token into Wren's palm whenever a pair is restored.
npcs.appearance: A short, broad spirit in a porter's vest and pillbox cap, brass tags clipped along his belt and lapels. His outline shimmers like steam off a kettle; his hands, though translucent, hold the cases firmly.

quirks: hums to the cases as he sorts them
polishes each tag with the cuff of his vest
tips his cap to luggage as well as people
personality.speech_pattern: kind, slow, sentences ending on a soft uplift

relationships.description: Pressed her first brass token into her palm and remembers the moment though she does not.
Defers to the Stationmaster's protocol but disagrees quietly about the timetables.
Keeps her case set aside on the topmost shelf, dusted weekly, never tagged.

entries.activity: presses tokens into Wren's palm and dims the lantern

idle: Someone meant to come back for you.
greeting: Ah. The clockmaker. Right on time, as always.
matching: There — that one's yours, isn't it?
A coat. A paperback. A packed lunch. Yes.
token: The chute will open for you now.

npcs.name: The Last Passenger
npcs.description: A young spirit in travel coat and scarf who waits on Platform 3½ with a sliding-tile timetable that never quite resolves. She offers Wren a new phantom ticket each night and never quite explains where she meant to go.
npcs.appearance: A slender figure on a bench, knees together, a folded travel coat across her lap. Her scarf catches the parallax steam as if alive. The timetable in her hands clicks and shifts of its own accord; her edges blur the longer you look.

quirks: hums fragments of a lullaby she can't finish
presses each phantom ticket flat with her thumb before handing it over
watches the skylight as if reading it
personality.speech_pattern: lilting, full of half-rhymes, often a beat behind the question

relationships.description: Sits closer to Wren than to anyone else. Will not say why.
Knows her case sits dusted on the topmost shelf, and is glad of it.
Tips her chin to him from the platform but will not enter the office.

entries.activity: watches the skylight, shuffles the timetable
listens for the whistle that almost answers

idle: Almost a whistle. Almost a hand on my shoulder.
timetable: Slide this one — no, the other. Yes.
A ticket for you. Don't read the destination too closely.
whistle: There. Did you hear it? It almost answered.

npcs.name: The Arrival Clock
npcs.description: Not quite an NPC, not quite a machine — the Arrival Clock in the Waiting Hall has a voice of its own, soft as a pendulum tick. It greets Wren at the start of every run and counts down the moon meter in a whisper only she can hear.
npcs.appearance: A vast brass-and-glass clock mounted above the departure boards, its pendulum stopped at 11:59. When Wren winds it the face glows faintly lantern-amber and the second hand begins its slow sweep.

fears: a moon that does not cross
personality.speech_pattern: metronomic, sentences clipped to the beat of a pendulum

relationships.description: Wound by her hands every night. Will run for no one else.

items.name: Mainspring Charge
items.description: A coiled brass spring humming with stored tension, spent to rewind broken clocks across the station.

effects.name: Rewind Clock
effects.description: Spend one charge to rewind a broken clock and nudge an adjacent room's puzzle state by one step.

items.lore_text: Wren keeps a tin of these in her apron pocket. Each one was wound by a clockmaker who is no longer in the world.
items.icon_description: A small coiled brass spring resting on aged cream paper, lantern-amber highlight catching the inner curl

items.name: Brass Oil Can
items.description: A long-spouted oil can that softens the resolution of any single puzzle, smoothing tile slides and dial turns.

effects.name: Easing Drop
effects.description: Apply a single drop to convert the next puzzle's hardest constraint into its softer variant for this run.

items.lore_text: The label has worn away, but the smell of warm brass and clove oil tells Wren everything she needs to know.
items.icon_description: A slender brass oil can with a curved spout, a single amber droplet suspended at the tip

items.name: Tuning Fork
items.description: A silvered tuning fork that, when struck against a rail, reveals the hidden order of luggage tags and timetable tiles.

effects.name: Resonant Hint
effects.description: Strike to briefly chime the correct next move in the current puzzle — one memory pair or one tile slide.

items.lore_text: Calibrated to the pitch of the 12:00 whistle. Wren has never heard the whistle herself, but the fork remembers.
items.icon_description: A two-pronged silver tuning fork, its tips faintly glowing midnight-blue against aged paper

items.name: Pendulum Weight
items.description: A heavy brass bob that, hung in any room, slows the moon meter's tick for the duration of one puzzle.

effects.name: Hung Bob
effects.description: Hang the weight to slow the moon meter by 25% while solving the current room's puzzle.

items.lore_text: Heavier than it looks. Wren swears she can feel the moon hesitating whenever it swings.
items.icon_description: A polished brass pendulum bob on a short chain, catching warm lantern light

items.name: Porter's Brass Token
items.description: A small engraved token the Porter presses into Wren's palm when memory pairs are restored. Opens the luggage chute to Platform 3½.

effects.name: Unlock Luggage Chute
effects.description: Unlocks the hidden chute connecting Lost Luggage to Platform 3½.

items.lore_text: Stamped with a name no one will say aloud. The Porter only hands it to those who matched the case to its owner.
items.icon_description: A round brass token, its rim worn smooth, a single tag-shaped notch cut into the face

items.name: Signal Pass
items.description: A folded paper pass embossed with the Stationmaster's stopped-clock seal. Opens the maintenance hatch beneath the departure boards.

effects.name: Unlock Maintenance Hatch
effects.description: Unlocks the hidden shortcut from the Waiting Hall directly into the Signal Box.

items.lore_text: The Stationmaster signs each one with the same fountain pen he used the night the 12:00 train failed to arrive.
items.icon_description: A folded cream paper pass, ink-drawn stopped-clock seal pressed in midnight-blue wax

items.name: Engraved Cog
items.description: A small brass cog inscribed with the date of a completed repair. Engraved into the workshop ledger floor at the end of each run.

effects.name: Ledger Engraving
effects.description: Banked between runs in the Conductor's Office floor; unlocks new starting tools and softer puzzle variants on future runs.

items.lore_text: A night that almost became whole. Wren reads the dates with her thumb whenever a run feels heavy.
items.icon_description: A small brass cog with a date engraved across its face, set against worn workshop floorboards

items.name: Banked Moonlight
items.description: A glass vial of pale moonlight banked when a spirit's request is fulfilled. Carries forward to the next run as starting moon meter time.

effects.name: Bank Moonlight
effects.description: Adds 45 seconds to the next run's moon meter when carried across the workshop ledger.

items.lore_text: The Last Passenger says moonlight tastes like a station you almost remembered.
items.icon_description: A slim glass vial of softly glowing pale-blue liquid, corked with brass and aged paper label

items.name: Humming Travel Case
items.description: A small leather case that hums faintly when carried near its owner's belongings. Used to complete the Porter's memory pairs.

effects.name: Owner Resonance
effects.description: Hums louder as Wren approaches the matching tag in Lost Luggage, narrowing memory-match pairs.

items.lore_text: Each case holds a folded coat, a paperback, a packed lunch — small proofs that someone meant to come back.
items.icon_description: A small worn leather case with a brass clasp and a paper tag, soft motion lines suggesting a hum

items.name: Stationmaster's Riddle Card
items.description: A stiff cream card hand-lettered with one of the Stationmaster's riddles. Solved cards become engraved cogs.

effects.name: Solve Riddle
effects.description: Turn in a solved riddle card to the Stationmaster to bank an engraved cog into the workshop ledger.

items.lore_text: The Stationmaster keeps a stack in his desk drawer. He claims he doesn't know the answers himself anymore.
items.icon_description: A cream cardstock rectangle with a hand-lettered ink riddle and a stopped-clock watermark

items.name: Phantom Ticket
items.description: A ticket stub for the 12:00 train that never quite arrives. Stamped with a destination that changes when no one is looking.

effects.name: Timetable Anchor
effects.description: Hold during a sliding-tile timetable puzzle to lock one tile of Wren's choosing in place.

items.lore_text: The Last Passenger carries one in every pocket. She offers Wren a new stub each night and never quite explains where she meant to go.
items.icon_description: A pale paper ticket stub with smudged midnight-blue ink, edges softened from being held too long

style_guide.art_style: Hand-pixeled 2D at a 64x64 sprite base for characters and key props, with 32x32 tile units for floors/walls and 128x128 reserved for hero set-pieces (Arrival Clock, Workshop Ledger floor, Great Skylight). Target render resolution: 384x216 internal canvas upscaled 5x to 1920x1080 with integer scaling, no sub-pixel filtering. Sprites use a strict 24-color global palette per scene with selective dithering (Bayer 4x4) only on glass and steam edges. Character silhouettes read at 3 tiles tall (Wren ~40px), with brass-loupe and apron-buckle as silhouette anchors. Animations: 8-frame idle breathing loops at 8fps, 6-frame winding loops at 12fps, 4-frame pendulum sways at 6fps, 12-frame steam puffs at 10fps for parallax layers, and 24-frame moon-meter sweep cycles tied to the 12-minute timer. UI is ink-on-aged-paper: hand-drawn at 2x pixel scale with 1px sepia outlines (#3a2a1c), drop-shadowed onto a paper texture overlay set to multiply at 35% opacity. Lantern bloom is achieved with a 3-pass additive blur on amber light sources (radius 2px, 4px, 8px) clamped to a 50% alpha ceiling so it never crushes the palette. Two parallax steam layers move at 0.25x and 0.6x camera speed; foreground gear-shadows pass at 1.4x. No anti-aliasing on sprite edges; all rotations are pre-baked at 8 cardinal angles to preserve the hand-pixeled feel.
color_palette: #e8d9b8 — aged paper cream (UI background, riddle cards)
#2a1a1a — true black (reserved for ink details and silhouette punch only)
style_guide.mood: Hushed, melancholic, and quietly hopeful — the visual feeling of a quiet platform at midnight where every brass fitting is dimmed but still warm, every pane of glass holds a held breath, and the lantern light promises that nothing here is hostile, only waiting. Steam drifts slow enough to count, pendulums sway in long arcs, and even the broken clocks tick once when looked at. The palette never goes fully black or fully white; the station exists in the soft margin between sleep and waking.
reference_games: Eastward (Pixpil) — for warm pixel lighting, parallax interiors, and gentle ambient storytelling
A Short Hike (adamgryu) — for hushed cozy pacing and quiet world tone
Inscryption (Daniel Mullins) — for ink-on-paper UI and hand-lettered card aesthetics
Spiritfarer (Thunder Lotus) — for melancholic-hopeful tone and tender NPC framing
Return of the Obra Dinn (Lucas Pope) — for 1-bit-adjacent restraint and brass/sepia mood (palette only, not 1-bit)
Loop Hero (Four Quarters) — for 64x64 hand-pixeled clarity at low resolution
Stardew Valley (ConcernedApe) — for lantern bloom, parallax depth, and readable indoor pixel scenes
The Case of the Golden Idol — for ink-and-aged-paper UI typography and hand-drawn frames
Strange Horticulture — for cozy-melancholic mood with quiet desk-scale interactions
Carto — for soft warm interiors and gentle puzzle pacing visuals
style_guide.line_weight: 1px sepia (#3a2a1c) outlines on UI elements and riddle cards; sprites use no outlines, relying on palette contrast and 1-pixel rim-light on brass edges (lantern-amber #f4d98a) for silhouette readability. Spirits have a deliberately broken 1-pixel outline (#d8e0ec) that fades every 3 frames to read as translucent. Architectural tiles use no outlines — depth is communicated through 2-step shadow ramps (midnight #1a1f3a → dusk #2d3656 → moon #4a5681).
style_guide.texture_style: Hand-pixeled with deliberate hand-placed dither only on glass surfaces (Bayer 4x4), steam edges (scattered noise), and spirit volumes (vertical-streak dither at 25% density). Brass is rendered with 3-step shadow ramps and a single hand-placed specular pixel per curve — never gradients, never auto-shading. Wood paneling uses 2-pixel horizontal grain repeated every 8px with hand-broken irregularity. Aged paper UI has a baked low-frequency noise overlay (multiply, 20% opacity) and hand-drawn fold creases at card corners. Floor tiles in the Conductor's Office show engraved cog patterns as 1-pixel-deep recessed shading — these accumulate visibly across runs as the persistent ledger fills.
style_guide.lighting: Warm-key, cool-fill, single-source per room. Lantern-amber (#f4d98a) primary lights cast a 3-pass additive bloom (2px/4px/8px radius, 50% alpha ceiling) with a 16-tile falloff to midnight-blue ambient (#1a1f3a). The Great Skylight in the Waiting Hall casts a moving moon-blue (#4a5681) shaft that sweeps across the floor over the 12-minute moon meter — 1 tile every 30 seconds, baked as 24 keyframes. Spirits emit no light themselves but pick up edge-fill from the nearest lantern, with their translucent fill (#b8c4d6) shifting 1 palette step warmer when within 3 tiles of an amber source. Platform 3½ uses a phantom-teal (#5a8a9a) secondary fill from off-screen, half the intensity of the main lantern, to mark it as not-quite-real. No room is ever lit above 70% perceptual brightness; the station is always dim, always warm, always waiting.

issues.description: No scenes or scripts have been generated yet (scenes_generated and scripts_generated are both empty arrays). The project is a design document but lacks any actual playable Godot scenes or GDScript implementation. Without these, the game cannot be launched or playtested.
issues.suggested_fix: Generate Godot scene files (.tscn) for each of the 5 rooms and GDScript files for core systems: moon meter timer, mainspring charge resource, three puzzle types (memory match, sliding tile, riddle), and the persistent ledger save system.

issues.description: stat_system and combat_system are null. While the concept correctly states 'no combat,' there is no defined progression/resource system schema for mainspring charges, moonlight banking, engraved cog counts, or persistent unlocks. Without a formalized resource system, the meta-progression loop has no defined data model.
issues.suggested_fix: Define a minimal stat_system describing mainspring_charges (per-run pool), moon_meter_seconds (per-run timer), engraved_cogs (persistent count), banked_moonlight (persistent vials), and unlocked starting tools. Leave combat_system as null intentionally with a comment.

issues.description: The Stationmaster's riddle puzzle has no described mechanic — quest_engrave_the_ledger requires delivering a 'solved' riddle card, but no objective explains HOW the player solves the riddle (multiple choice? typed answer? card-matching?). All other spirits have defined puzzle types (memory_match, sliding_tile_timetable) but riddle resolution is hand-waved.
issues.suggested_fix: Specify a riddle interaction: e.g., multiple-choice card selection from 3 hand-lettered options, or symbol-matching the riddle's clue to an item from inventory (Wren's pocket items).

issues.description: Mainspring charge economy is undefined. quest_set_the_signal_levers requires spending at least 3 charges, but Wren starts with only 3 in her inventory and no quest defines how charges replenish during a run. If charges are consumed at Signal Box (3) plus the Arrival Clock wind (1), the player runs out before completing the loop.
issues.suggested_fix: Add a Mainspring Dispenser interaction at entity_mainspring_dispenser in the Signal Box, or grant charges as rewards from each spirit puzzle. Verify that 4-6 charges per run is the intended budget.

issues.description: Two hidden/locked connections (Waiting Hall ↔ Signal Box via signal_pass, Lost Luggage ↔ Platform 3½ via porter_token) are described as shortcuts, but quest_engrave_the_ledger lists obj_earn_signal_pass as OPTIONAL and the porter token as a required reward of quest_match_the_humming_cases. The shortcut keys are inconsistently gated — one is optional, one is required for the same loop-shortening benefit.
issues.suggested_fix: Either make both keys optional (rewards for excellence) or both mandatory (always granted on first puzzle clear). Clarify whether shortcuts persist across runs.

issues.description: No HUD specification exists for the always-visible moon meter (12-minute countdown), current mainspring charge count, active drafted tool, or engraved-cog total. These are all core mechanics the player must reference constantly.
issues.location: style_guide (UI section), no dedicated hud entity
issues.suggested_fix: Add a HUD spec describing: top-right ink-on-paper moon meter ring tied to the 24-keyframe skylight sweep, top-left charge counter (tin icon + number), bottom-center drafted-tool slot with hover tooltip, and pause-menu workshop ledger view.

warnings: The 12-minute moon meter is tight for first-time players solving three distinct puzzle types — playtest the first-run completion rate; if under 30% reach all three spirits, increase starting moonlight or add a tutorial-night softening.
Spirit dialogue trees are referenced by ID (e.g., dialogue_stationmaster_riddle) but no dialogue tree content is included in the project payload — these need to be authored.

Five rooms with shuffle_each_run=true plus three puzzle types plus tool drafting plus persistent unlocks is ambitious scope for 4 hours of estimated playtime; verify run variance is meaningful enough to sustain replays.
Platform 3½ phantom-teal lighting and the 'breaks 1-pixel outline every 3 frames' spirit shader are non-trivial to implement in Godot's 2D pipeline — budget time for a custom CanvasItem shader.
suggestions: Add an explicit 'first-night' tutorial state where Wren has all three tools pre-drafted and the moon meter is paused during dialogue, easing new-player onboarding into the 12-minute pressure.
Consider a sixth 'Workshop' overworld room (separate from Conductor's Office) as the persistent meta hub between runs, so the in-run Conductor's Office stays purely diegetic.

Author the Stationmaster's riddles as a pool of 20-30 hand-lettered cards so repeat runs feel handcrafted rather than randomized; tie answers to ambient station details (e.g., 'I have hands but never wave — Arrival Clock').

Add quiet failure-state-adjacent feedback: when the moon meter expires mid-puzzle, fade to soft ink-wash with Wren saying 'Almost. Tomorrow, then.' rather than a hard fail screen — matches the 'no failure state' design promise.
The Banked Moonlight max_stack of 3 (45s each = 135s) is a thoughtful cap, but make sure UI surfaces this clearly so players know hoarding past 3 vials is wasted.
Pre-bake the 8-cardinal-angle sprite rotations as part of the asset pipeline rather than per-frame, since the style guide forbids runtime rotation.
qa_report.summary: Strong, cohesive cozy roguelike design with a clear vision, rich worldbuilding, and well-aligned art/audio/mechanics — but the project is currently a design document only. No scenes or scripts have been generated, so it is not yet playable. Once the Godot implementation is produced and the riddle mechanic + charge economy are specified, this is a 9/10 candidate; as a design pass it is an 8, marked down to 7 because the unstated puzzle resolution for the Stationmaster and the unbalanced mainspring economy will block the first build.
